title: An Examen With No Cycle to Review
reflection:
For years the Examen had a familiar shape to look back on — a month's rhythm to trace, phase by phase, for where God had moved. That shape is gone now, and the review must find a new one.

This isn't the end of noticing. It's noticing turned toward a different kind of day: not where am I in the cycle, but simply, where am I, today, right now.
closing: Teach me to examine a life with no cycle to trace. Meet me in the plain shape of today. Amen.

scripture.text: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?

title: What the Reviewing Taught
reflection:
Every month you once reviewed, every consolation and desolation you learned to name by feel — none of that discernment was wasted. It trained an attentiveness that outlasts the cycle that shaped it.

Look back today with gratitude rather than grief. The skill of noticing where God moves in you is yours now, permanently, however differently your days are counted.
closing: Thank you for the discernment those years built in me. Let it walk with me still. Amen.

scripture.text: Hitherto the Lord has helped us.

title: Neither Consolation nor Desolation, Only Today
reflection:
No monthly swing to track between fullness and depletion — just an ordinary day, its movements quieter than they've been in years.

There may be a mourning in that quiet, and a peace in it too. Ignatius never asked you to choose only one feeling per season. Let today hold both, without forcing a verdict.
closing: In this quieter day, hold both what I miss and what I'm grateful for. You have room for both. Amen.

scripture.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

title: Discernment Without a Frame
reflection:
No phase to name, no cycle to locate yourself within — just the plain work of noticing where you are drawn and where you pull back, same as always, minus the frame you used to hang it on.

That can feel disorienting before it feels spacious. Let the discernment widen rather than disappear: it was never really about the frame. It was always about paying attention.
closing: Widen my discernment to fit this open country. Teach me to notice you here as surely as I did before. Amen.

scripture.text: You will show me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy.

title: The Same God Who Reads the Examen
reflection:
Cycles change. The rhythms you once tracked change. What has met you in every review, every honest accounting, has not.

However unfamiliar this stretch of noticing feels, the One who illuminated your Examen in the old rhythm illuminates it still, in whatever shape today takes.
closing: Thank you for staying the same companion through every way I've learned to notice you. Illuminate this day too. Amen.

scripture.text: I am with you always, to the end of the age.
